CAB Policy Document 2024-01: Biosafety Management Policy
Document type/version: Policy Document

1.1 This policy establishes the framework for the safe handling, storage, transfer, and disposal of biological agents and toxins within all facilities under the purview of the Centre for Advanced Biosciences (CAB).

1.2 The policy is intended to protect personnel, the public, and the environment from biological hazards while supporting the legitimate research and teaching activities of the Centre.

1.3 All activities involving biological materials shall be conducted in accordance with the Singapore Biosafety Guidelines and the Biological Agents and Toxins Act (BATA) and its subsidiary legislation.

**2. Scope**

2.1 This policy applies to all CAB staff, students, visiting researchers, contractors, and any other persons engaged in work within CAB laboratories or using CAB-controlled biological materials.

2.2 The policy covers all work involving:
   (a) Human, animal, and plant pathogens;
   (b) Genetically modified organisms (GMOs) and genetically modified micro-organisms (GMMOs);
   (c) Biological toxins;
   (d) Human and primate cell lines, tissues, and blood products;
   (e) Any other biological material determined by the Biosafety Committee to present a biosafety risk.

2.3 This policy does not apply to:
   (a) Chemical safety matters, which are governed by the Chemical Safety Policy (CAB-POL-2023-07);
   (b) Radiation safety matters, which are governed by the Radiation Safety Policy (CAB-POL-2023-09);
   (c) Clinical activities conducted by the associated teaching hospital, which fall under hospital policy.

**3. Definitions**

3.1 **Biological Agent**: Any micro-organism, cell culture, or human endoparasite, including any that have been genetically modified, which may cause infection, allergy, toxicity, or otherwise pose a risk to human health.

3.2 **Biosafety Level (BSL)**: The containment level required for work with biological agents, as defined in the WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual, ranging from BSL-1 (lowest risk) to BSL-4 (highest risk).

3.3 **Biosafety Committee (BSC)**: The committee established by CAB to oversee biosafety matters, approve work with biological agents, and ensure compliance with this policy.

3.4 **Centre for Advanced Biosciences (CAB)**: The administrative unit to which the laboratories and facilities covered by this policy belong.

3.5 **Office of Safety, Health and Environment (OSHE)**: The office responsible for the day-to-day implementation of safety policies, including biosafety, across CAB.

3.6 **Principal Investigator (PI)**: The individual responsible for the scientific direction and operational conduct of a research group or laboratory within CAB.

3.7 **Biological Materials**: Any biological agent, toxin, GMO, or material containing or derived from the above, including clinical samples, environmental isolates, and research stocks.

3.8 **Containment**: The combination of physical, operational, and procedural measures used to prevent the release of biological agents from a laboratory or facility.

**4. General Biosafety Principles**

4.1 **Risk Assessment**: No work with biological materials shall commence until a documented risk assessment has been completed and approved. The risk assessment shall consider the hazard group of the agent, the proposed manipulations, the volume and concentration of material, the potential for aerosol generation, and the competence of personnel.

5.5 OSHE shall issue a written inspection report within two weeks of each inspection. The Principal Investigator of the affected laboratory shall respond in writing to the report, confirming the actions taken or proposed. OSHE shall follow up to verify that corrective actions have been completed.

**6. Training Requirements**

6.1 No person shall undertake work involving biological materials unless they have completed the mandatory biosafety training prescribed by OSHE and approved by the BSC.

6.2 The mandatory training shall cover, at a minimum:

a) The principles of risk assessment and the hazard groups of biological agents;

b) Safe handling practices, including aseptic technique, the use of biological safety cabinets, and the prevention of aerosol generation;

c) The correct use of personal protective equipment;

d) Decontamination, disinfection, and sterilisation procedures;

e) Waste handling and disposal requirements;

f) Emergency procedures, including spill response and exposure management;

g) The requirements of this policy and of the related CAB-SOP-2024-01 (Standard Operating Procedures for Work with Biological Materials).

6.3 Refresher training shall be completed at least once every two years. OSHE shall maintain a training register and shall notify personnel and their Principal Investigators at least one month before a training record is due to expire.
f) Any deviation from the requirements in this Section, including the temporary storage of waste beyond the periods specified in CAB-SOP-2024-01, shall require prior written approval from OSHE. OSHE shall consult the BSC where the deviation is expected to last more than 48 hours.

**3. Clarification of Responsibilities**

Version 2.0 includes minor editorial changes to clarify the responsibilities of Principal Investigators and laboratory supervisors. These changes do not alter the substantive obligations in Version 1.0 but are intended to remove ambiguity in the following areas:

a) Section 5.2 (d) is amended to state that the Principal Investigator is responsible for ensuring that all laboratory personnel, including visiting researchers and students, have completed the required training before commencing work. The previous wording referred only to "personnel".

b) Section 5.3 (b) is amended to clarify that the laboratory supervisor shall be responsible for the daily inspection of biological safety cabinets and for reporting any malfunction to OSHE. The previous wording did not specify who was responsible for reporting.

**4. Transitional Arrangements**

The following transitional arrangements shall apply from the Effective Date until 31 December 2024:

a) Laboratories that have existing waste disposal contracts that do not comply with Section 2 of this Policy shall have until 31 December 2024 to renegotiate those contracts. OSHE shall provide a list of approved waste contractors to assist laboratories in this process.

b) Training records that were due for renewal under Version 1.0 between the Effective Date and 31 August 2025 shall be renewed in accordance with the new two-year interval. OSHE shall calculate the new expiry dates and shall communicate them to the affected personnel.

c) Any laboratory that has been granted an exemption under Version 1.0 shall have its exemption reviewed by the BSC within six months of the Effective Date. The review shall consider whether the exemption remains appropriate in light of the changes in this Policy.

**6. Review of this Policy**

This Policy shall be reviewed by the BSC at least once every three years from the Effective Date, or earlier if there are significant changes to relevant legislation, national guidelines, or the nature of work undertaken by CAB. Any proposed amendments shall be submitted to the BSC for approval before being incorporated into a new version of this Policy.

### 2. Definitions

For the purposes of this policy:

- **Biorisk**: The combination of the probability of occurrence of harm and the severity of that harm, where the source of harm is a biological agent or toxin.
- **Biorisk Management**: A systematic approach to controlling biorisks, including risk assessment, risk mitigation, and performance monitoring.
- **Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC)**: A primary containment device that provides personnel, product, and environmental protection through HEPA filtration and directional airflow.
- **Competency Assessment**: A documented evaluation of an individual's ability to perform specific tasks safely and correctly.
- **Laboratory Safety Officer (LSO)**: The individual designated by the IBC to oversee day-to-day biosafety compliance, training coordination, and biorisk assessment activities.
- **PPE**: Personal Protective Equipment.

---

### 3. Biorisk Management

#### 3.1 General Principles

CAB adopts a biorisk management approach that considers the full range of risks associated with biological materials, including risks to personnel, the community, and the environment. This approach is based on the following principles:

a) Risk assessment shall be conducted before any new activity involving biological agents is initiated, and shall be reviewed whenever there is a significant change in the activity, the agents used, or the facility.

b) Risk mitigation measures shall be proportionate to the level of risk identified and shall follow the hierarchy of controls: elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, and PPE.

c) Biorisk assessments shall be documented and retained for at least five years. The LSO shall maintain a register of all completed assessments.

#### 3.2 Risk Assessment Process

The risk assessment process shall include:

a) Identification of all biological agents and toxins present or potentially present in the sample or material;

b) Consideration of the agent's pathogenicity, virulence, route of transmission, and infectious dose;

c) Evaluation of the experimental procedures, including potential for aerosol generation, sharps use, and volume of material handled;

d) Assessment of personnel competency and training status;

e) Review of facility design and engineering controls, including BSC certification status and laboratory ventilation;

f) Identification of any additional risks, such as the presence of allergens, adventitious agents, or antibiotic resistance markers.

#### 3.3 Risk Mitigation

Following risk assessment, the following measures shall be applied as appropriate:

a) Use of the lowest possible biosafety level that is consistent with safe work;

b) Implementation of standard microbiological practices and, where required, additional special practices;

c) Use of appropriate containment equipment, including BSCs and centrifuge safety cups;

d) Restriction of access to the laboratory to authorised personnel only;

e) Posting of biohazard warning signs at laboratory entrances;

f) Development of activity-specific standard operating procedures (SOPs) when the risk assessment indicates a need.
d) For incidents involving agents requiring BSL-3 containment, the LSO shall notify the CAB Director and the Office of Safety, Health and Environment (OSHE) immediately upon becoming aware of the incident.

e) The person(s) involved shall not resume work until cleared by the LSO or a designated safety officer.

##### 4.3 Reporting Procedure

All incidents and near-misses shall be recorded in the CAB Incident Report Log (CAB-IRL). The initial report shall include at minimum:

a) Date and time of the incident;

b) Location, including laboratory room number and BSC number if applicable;

c) Names of persons involved or exposed;

d) Description of the incident, including the biological agent or toxin involved, if known;

e) Immediate actions taken; and

f) Whether medical attention was sought.

The initial report may be submitted verbally to the LSO, but shall be followed by a written report via the CAB-IRL within 24 hours. Where the person involved is unable to submit the report, the LSO or a designated deputy shall do so on their behalf.

###### 4.3.2 External Reporting

The LSO, in consultation with the CAB Director and OSHE, shall determine whether the incident is notifiable to external authorities. Notifications shall be made in accordance with:

a) The Biological Agents and Toxins Act, for incidents involving regulated biological agents;

b) The Workplace Safety and Health Act, for incidents resulting in personal injury or dangerous occurrences;

c) The Ministry of Health, for incidents involving potential transmission of infectious diseases; and

d) Any other applicable statutory requirements.

The LSO shall maintain a record of all external notifications, including the date and time of notification, the authority notified, and the reference number assigned.

##### 4.4 Investigation

a) The LSO, who shall chair the investigation;

b) A representative from OSHE;

c) The Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor responsible for the affected area;

d) A member of the Biosafety Committee, where the incident involves regulated biological agents or where the risk assessment indicates a potential for significant harm; and

##### 5. Audits and Inspections

###### 5.1 Purpose

The University shall establish and maintain a programme of audits and inspections to verify that the requirements of this Policy, the Biosafety Management System, and relevant statutory obligations are being implemented effectively. The audit programme is intended to identify gaps, non-conformities, and opportunities for improvement, and to confirm that risk controls remain adequate.

###### 5.2 Internal Audits

Internal audits shall be conducted by the Office of Safety, Health and Environment (OSHE) in accordance with the annual audit plan approved by the CAB Director. The audit plan shall be risk-based, taking into account the biosafety risk level of activities, the history of incidents and non-conformities, and any significant changes to facilities, equipment, or personnel.

a) The frequency of internal audits shall be as follows:

i) Containment facilities operating at Biosafety Level 3 (BSL-3) or Animal Biosafety Level 3 (ABSL-3): at least once every 12 months;

ii) Containment facilities operating at Biosafety Level 2 (BSL-2): at least once every 24 months;

iii) Laboratories conducting work with regulated biological agents under the Biological Agents and Toxins Act (BATA): at least once every 12 months; and

iv) Other laboratories and support areas: at least once every 36 months, or more frequently where the risk assessment indicates a need.

The CAB Director may direct additional audits at any time where there is reasonable cause, including in response to an incident, a significant non-conformity, or a change in legislation.

###### 5.3 Audit Team and Independence

Audits shall be conducted by auditors who are competent in biosafety and biosecurity matters and who are independent of the activity being audited. OSHE shall maintain a list of approved internal auditors, and shall ensure that auditors have no direct responsibility for the area under audit. Where the required expertise is not available internally, the CAB Director may engage an external auditor with the approval of the Biosafety Committee.

###### 5.4 Audit Process

Each audit shall include:

a) A review of relevant documents, including risk assessments, SOPs, training records, and maintenance logs;

b) A physical inspection of the facility, including containment barriers, ventilation systems, waste handling, and security measures;

c) Interviews with the Principal Investigator, laboratory staff, and other relevant personnel;

d) Verification that the requirements of this Policy and applicable SOPs are being followed in practice; and

e) A review of incident and near-miss reports, and the status of corrective actions previously identified.

The audit team shall record all findings, including observations, opportunities for improvement, and non-conformities. Non-conformities shall be classified as critical, major, or minor in accordance with the classification criteria set out in the Biosafety Management System manual.

###### 5.5 Audit Report

The audit team shall prepare a written audit report within 15 working days of the completion of the audit. The report shall include:

a) The scope and objectives of the audit;

b) The names of the auditors and the dates of the audit;

c) A summary of the activities and areas audited;

d) A detailed list of findings, including the classification of each non-conformity;

e) The root cause of each non-conformity, where it can be reasonably established; and
###### 5.6 Follow-Up and Closure

Corrective actions identified in an audit report shall be tracked in the Biosafety Management System action log. The Principal Investigator or other responsible person named in the report shall submit a written response within 10 working days of receiving the report, stating the corrective actions taken or planned, and the target date for completion.

The audit team, or a nominee of the CAB Director, shall verify the implementation of corrective actions within 30 working days of the stated completion date. Where verification confirms that the corrective actions have been effectively implemented, the non-conformity shall be closed and recorded as such in the action log. Where implementation is found to be incomplete or ineffective, the matter shall be escalated to the Biosafety Committee for further direction.

The CAB Director shall review the audit findings and the status of corrective actions at least once per quarter, and shall report significant trends or recurring non-conformities to the Biosafety Committee.

#### 6. TRANSPORT OF BIOLOGICAL MATERIALS

###### 6.1 Scope

This Section applies to the transport of biological materials, including infectious substances, diagnostic specimens, genetically modified organisms, and other materials that may present a risk to human health, animal health, or the environment, within the University campus, between University premises, and to or from external parties.

Transport includes movement by road, rail, air, or sea, and includes the transfer of materials between laboratories, to or from storage facilities, and to or from collaborating institutions, couriers, or waste disposal contractors.

###### 6.2 General Requirements

All transport of biological materials shall be conducted in accordance with the applicable national and international regulations, including the Singapore Infectious Diseases Act, the UN Model Regulations, the International Air Transport Association (IATA) Dangerous Goods Regulations, and the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Technical Instructions.

The shipper of any biological material is responsible for:

a) Determining the correct classification of the material, including the UN number, proper shipping name, and packing group, where applicable;

b) Confirming that the material is correctly packaged and labelled;

c) Preparing the required documentation, including the shipper's declaration and any permits or licences; and

d) Ensuring that the transport is undertaken by an approved carrier and that the recipient is authorised to receive the material.

The Principal Investigator or Laboratory Manager shall ensure that all staff involved in the preparation, packaging, or dispatch of biological materials are trained in the relevant requirements before carrying out any transport-related duties. Training shall be recorded in accordance with the training record CAB-TR.

###### 6.3 Classification of Biological Materials

For the purposes of this Policy, biological materials transported off campus shall be classified as follows:

| Category | Description | Examples |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Category A | Infectious substances transported in a form that, when exposure to it occurs, is capable of causing permanent disability, life-threatening or fatal disease in otherwise healthy humans or animals | Cultures of pathogens assigned to Risk Group 3 or 4 |
| Category B | Infectious substances that do not meet the criteria for inclusion in Category A | Clinical specimens and cultures of Risk Group 2 agents |
| Exempt | Materials that are unlikely to cause disease in humans or animals, or that have been treated to eliminate pathogens | Fixed tissues, nucleic acid extracts, non-infectious cell lines |

**7. Policy Review, Amendment, and Version Control**

**7.1 Purpose of This Section**

This section establishes the procedures for reviewing, amending, and versioning this Policy. The intent is to ensure that the Policy remains current, accurate, and aligned with national legislation, international standards, and the operational needs of the University. All amendments, whether substantive or editorial, shall be processed and recorded in accordance with this section.

**7.2 Scheduled Review Cycle**

The Policy shall be subject to a formal review at least once every three years from the date of the last comprehensive review. The next scheduled review shall be completed no later than 15 January 2028.

The Biosafety Committee (BSC) shall initiate the review. The BSC may, at its discretion, bring forward the review date if any of the following circumstances arise:

a) A significant incident involving biological materials occurs within the University or at another institution that reveals a gap or deficiency in this Policy;

b) A relevant national law, regulation, or code of practice is amended or introduced;

c) A relevant international guideline, such as those issued by the World Health Organization (WHO) Laboratory Biosafety Manual, is updated; or

d) The BSC otherwise determines that a review is necessary to address an emerging risk or operational issue.

**7.3 Initiation of Amendments**

Any member of the University community, including staff, students, and researchers, may propose an amendment to this Policy. Proposals shall be submitted in writing to the CAB Office using the Amendment Request Form (CAB-FM-07). The form shall include:

a) The name and contact details of the proposer;

b) The section(s) of the Policy to which the proposed amendment relates;

c) A clear statement of the proposed change, including the current text and the proposed revised text where practicable;

d) The rationale for the change, including any supporting evidence, references, or incident reports; and

e) The signature of the proposer and, where the proposer is a student, the endorsement of their Principal Investigator or Supervisor.

The CAB Office shall acknowledge receipt of the Amendment Request Form within five (5) working days. The CAB Office shall maintain a register of all amendment requests, which shall be reviewed by the BSC at its next scheduled meeting.

The BSC shall consider all amendment requests received. In reviewing a proposed amendment, the BSC shall have regard to:

4.2 Biosafety Officer (B. Tan) – Reviews this SOP annually, conducts audits, and investigates any breach of containment.

4.3 All Personnel – Must follow this SOP without deviation. Any deviation must be reported immediately to the Laboratory Manager and the Biosafety Officer.

CAB Standard Operating Procedure 2024-01 effective_date 2024-06-20 date. Record status: historical.

5. PPE REQUIREMENTS

The following PPE is mandatory for all personnel inside the BSL-3 laboratory:

- Disposable surgical scrubs (provided by CAB)
- Dedicated laboratory shoes (closed-toe, non-slip)
- Disposable boot covers
- Full-length, disposable gown (back-closing)
- Double gloves (inner nitrile, outer nitrile)
- N95 respirator (fit-tested) or powered air-purifying respirator (PAPR) if approved by the Biosafety Officer
- Full-face shield over the respirator

PPE must be donned in the order listed above and doffed in the reverse order, except that the outer gloves and gown are removed together in the airlock as described in Section 7.

6. ENTRY PROCEDURE

Entry into the BSL-3 laboratory is a two-stage process: preparation in the change room, followed by passage through the airlock.

6.1 Stage 1 – Preparation in the Change Room

1. Confirm that you have signed the entry logbook at the reception desk and that your name is listed on the daily access roster.
2. Remove all personal clothing and jewellery. Store them in your assigned locker.
3. Put on the disposable surgical scrubs. Ensure the scrubs are clean and free of any visible tears.
4. Put on the dedicated laboratory shoes.
5. Put on the N95 respirator. Perform a user seal check:
   - Cover the respirator with both hands and exhale sharply. If air leaks around the nose, adjust the nosepiece.
   - Cover the respirator with both hands and inhale. If the respirator collapses slightly, the seal is acceptable.
6. Put on the inner nitrile gloves.
7. Inspect the outer gloves, gown, boot covers, and face shield for any defects before proceeding to the airlock.
1. Complete your work and decontaminate all materials that will leave the laboratory (see Section 9, Waste Handling).
2. Approach the airlock from the laboratory side. Verify that the indicator light shows GREEN.
3. Open the inner door, step inside, and close the door fully behind you. Wait for the light to turn GREEN again.
4. Remove the outer gloves and the gown together. Peel the gown off from the shoulders, turning it inside out as you go, and place both items into the biohazard waste bin inside the airlock.
5. Remove the boot covers and place them into the same bin.
6. Remove the full-face shield and place it on the clean shelf for disinfection after exiting.
7. Open the outer door and step into the change room. Close the door behind you.
8. Proceed to Section 8, Doffing and Exit, for the remaining steps.

Note: If the alarm sounds while you are inside the airlock, remain still. Do not open either door. Wait for instructions from the Laboratory Manager or Biosafety Officer over the intercom.

8. DOFFING AND EXIT

1. In the change room, remove the inner nitrile gloves first. Dispose of them in the yellow biohazard bin.
2. Perform hand hygiene using the alcohol-based hand rub dispenser on the wall.
3. Remove the N95 respirator. Grasp the bottom strap, then the top strap, and lift the respirator away from your face without touching the front. Dispose of it in the yellow bin.
4. Remove the surgical scrubs and place them in the linen collection hamper labelled "CAB – LAUNDRY".
5. Remove the dedicated laboratory shoes and place them on the shoe rack. These shoes must not be worn outside the laboratory area.
6. Perform hand hygiene again.
7. Sign out in the exit logbook at the reception desk. Record the time of exit and confirm that you have not removed any items from the laboratory without prior authorisation.

9. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES

Emergency procedures apply to all personnel inside the BSL-3 laboratory. In the event of any emergency, the primary priority is the safety of personnel. Containment of the agent is secondary but must be addressed as soon as it is safe to do so.

9.1 Spill Response

CAB Standard Operating Procedure 2024-01 version_number 1.0 version. Record status: historical.

Spills are categorised according to the volume of the spill and the risk of aerosol generation.

1. Alert others in the laboratory by calling out "Spill on the bench" clearly.
2. Cover the spill with absorbent paper towels.
3. Carefully pour freshly prepared 1% sodium hypochlorite solution over the towels, working from the outside of the spill towards the centre.
4. Allow the disinfectant to remain in contact for at least 20 minutes.
5. Wipe up the spill with the towels and place them in the biohazard waste bin.
6. Wipe the area again with 70% ethanol.
7. Complete an entry in the incident report log CAB-IRL within 24 hours.

9.1.2 Large Spills (10 mL or More, or Any Aerosol)

1. Immediately leave the laboratory, following the exit procedure in Section 7.2. Do not attempt to clean the spill yourself.
2. Alert the Laboratory Manager and the Biosafety Officer by calling the emergency number 6772-8890 from a safe location.
3. Do not re-enter the laboratory until the Biosafety Officer has assessed the situation and given clearance.
4. The Biosafety Officer will coordinate the cleanup, which will be performed by trained personnel wearing full PPE and using a respirator.
5. Complete an entry in the incident report log CAB-IRL as soon as possible, but no later than 4 hours after the incident.

9.2 Evacuation
1. PPE requirements updated: double gloving is now mandatory for all work involving open
   manipulation of infectious material. Previously, double gloving was only required for
   procedures with a high risk of sharps injury or splashes.
2. The airlock entry sequence has been revised. The old sequence required personnel to don the
   laboratory gown before entering the airlock. In Version 2.0, the gown is donned inside the
   airlock, after the outer door is closed. This change is intended to reduce the risk of
   contamination of the corridor.
3. Exit procedure modified: the step requiring personnel to remove the inner gloves in the
   laboratory before entering the airlock has been removed. Both pairs of gloves are now removed
   in the airlock, after the inner door is closed.
4. The shoe cover step in the exit procedure has been clarified. Shoe covers are now removed in
   the airlock, not in the laboratory.
5. Section 7.2 (Exit) now includes a step to disinfect the outer surface of the airlock bench
   after use. This step was previously listed only in the daily cleaning schedule.
6. The emergency contact number in Section 9.1.2 has been updated to 6772-8890.

All personnel must read this SOP in full and acknowledge that they have understood the changes.
Acknowledgment forms are kept by the CAB office.

1. PURPOSE

This SOP describes the procedures for entry into and exit from the BSL-3 laboratory located on
Level 2 of the CAB Annex. The procedures are designed to prevent the release of biological agents
and to protect personnel from exposure.

2. SCOPE

This SOP applies to all personnel, including researchers, technicians, students, and visitors,
who require access to the BSL-3 laboratory. Access is granted only to personnel who have
completed the required biosafety training and have been approved by the Biosafety Officer.

3. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| BSL-3 | Biosafety Level 3 |
| CAB | Containment and Biosafety |
| PPE | Personal Protective Equipment |
| IRL | Incident Report Log |
| BSC | Biological Safety Cabinet |

4. REFERENCES

CAB Standard Operating Procedure 2025-01 effective_date 2025-03-01 date. Record status: current.

- CAB-POL-2025-01, Biosafety Policy for Containment Laboratories
- CAB-SOP-2024-02, Decontamination and Waste Management
- CAB-SOP-2024-03, Maintenance and Certification of Biological Safety Cabinets
- SS 632:2019, Code of Practice for Biosafety

5. PPE REQUIREMENTS

The following PPE must be worn by all personnel inside the BSL-3 laboratory. PPE is stored on
shelves outside the laboratory, on the left of the airlock entrance.

| Item | Quantity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Disposable gown (fluid-resistant) | 1 | Must be worn over laboratory clothing. |
| Inner gloves (nitrile) | 1 pair | Must be worn under the outer gloves. |
| Outer gloves (nitrile) | 1 pair | Must be worn over the cuffs of the gown. |
| Surgical mask | 1 | Must be worn at all times. |
| Shoe covers | 1 pair | Must be worn over closed-toe shoes. |
| Safety goggles or face shield | 1 | Must be worn when performing procedures that may generate splashes or aerosols. |

Double gloving is mandatory for all work involving open manipulation of infectious material.
This includes, but is not limited to, pipetting, vortexing, and opening tubes containing
concentrated cultures. For work that does not involve open manipulation, such as operating
equipment behind a closed front, single gloving is permitted.

6. ENTRY PROCEDURE

The entry procedure is a sequence of steps that must be followed in order. Do not skip steps.
If you are unsure about any step, stop and ask the Laboratory Manager or Biosafety Officer.

6.1 Before Entering the Laboratory Area
6.1 Before Entering the Laboratory Area

1. Remove all personal items (watches, jewellery, mobile phones, wallets) and place them in the
   personal lockers provided outside the laboratory. Lockers are located along the corridor
   opposite the main door, labelled A1 to A24.
2. Change out of outdoor footwear into the laboratory-issued closed-toe shoes kept on the shoe
   rack. Outdoor footwear must be placed in the shoe cubbies provided. Do not walk in socks or
   barefoot in this area.
3. Check the daily entry roster posted on the notice board to confirm that your name has been
   cleared for the day's work. If your name is not on the roster, do not proceed. Contact the
   Laboratory Manager for verification.
4. Review the risk assessment form CAB-RAF for the specific activity you will be performing. A
   copy of the current CAB-RAF is kept in the clear file holder next to the roster. If the
   activity you are about to perform is not covered by a current CAB-RAF, stop and inform the
   Biosafety Officer before proceeding.
5. Sign the entry logbook. Record the date, time of entry, your name (in block letters), and the
   purpose of entry. The logbook is located on the small table to the right of the airlock door.
   Use the pen attached to the table; do not bring pens into the laboratory.
6. Perform a visual inspection of the airlock anteroom. Check that the inner door is closed and
   the pressure differential gauge reads between -30 Pa and -50 Pa relative to the corridor.
   If the gauge reads outside this range, do not enter. Notify the Laboratory Manager
   immediately.
7. If you are entering to perform work involving open manipulation of infectious material,
   ensure that you have sufficient supplies for the entire session before entering. Once inside,
   do not exit and re-enter for supplies unless absolutely necessary.

6.2 Donning PPE

1. Collect the required PPE from the shelves outside the laboratory, on the left of the airlock
   entrance. Check the size and condition of each item. Discard any item that appears torn,
   perforated, or expired in the designated waste bin labelled "PPE waste".
2. Put on the disposable gown first. Ensure the gown covers the back and front of your body and
   that the ties are secured at the back. The gown must be long enough to cover your laboratory
   clothing completely.
3. Put on the shoe covers over your closed-toe shoes. Pull them up over the ankles. If you feel
   any tear, replace them before proceeding.
4. Put on the inner gloves (nitrile). Ensure they fit snugly. Do not wear rings or other
   jewellery under the gloves.
5. Put on the surgical mask. The mask must cover both your nose and mouth. Press the nose wire
   to fit the contour of your nose. Do not remove the mask while inside the laboratory.
6. Put on the safety goggles or face shield. Adjust the strap so that the goggles sit firmly but
   comfortably. If you wear prescription glasses, the goggles must fit over them without
   causing gaps.
7. Put on the outer gloves (nitrile). Tuck the cuffs of the gown into the outer gloves so that
   no skin is exposed at the wrists.
8. Perform a buddy check. Ask another person who is entering or a person already inside the
   laboratory to verify that your PPE is complete and that there are no gaps or exposed skin.
   If you are entering alone, use the full-length mirror mounted on the inside of the airlock
   door to perform the check yourself.
CAB Standard Operating Procedure 2024-01: BSL-3 Laboratory Entry and Exit

7. Documentation and Record-Keeping

7.1 Entry Log

1. Every person entering the BSL-3 laboratory must sign the entry log before donning PPE. The log is located on the clipboard holder immediately to the left of the airlock door, outside the laboratory.
2. Record the following information legibly in the designated columns:
   a. Date and time of entry (use the 24-hour clock, e.g. 09:15, 14:40)
   b. Full name and staff/student ID number
   c. Purpose of entry (e.g. routine culture work, equipment maintenance, cleaning)
   d. Time of exit
   e. Initials of the person performing the buddy check, if applicable
3. If you forget to sign in before entering, do not attempt to enter again solely to sign the log. Upon exiting, sign the log and clearly state the actual time of entry in the remarks column, and inform the Laboratory Manager within the same working day.
4. Do not leave blank columns. If a column is not applicable, write "N/A" in that column.
5. The entry log is a controlled document. Do not remove pages from the logbook. When a logbook is full, return it to the Laboratory Manager, who will archive it in the records room (Cabinet B, shelf 3).
6. Electronic entry logs may be maintained in place of the paper log, subject to prior approval by the Laboratory Manager. The electronic system must capture the same fields listed in clause 7.1.2 and must not allow retrospective edits without an audit trail.

7.2 Training Records

1. No person may enter the BSL-3 laboratory unless their training record, CAB-TR, shows a current and valid authorisation for entry.
2. Training records are maintained by the Laboratory Manager and are updated within five working days of the completion of any training session or refresher course.
3. The following entries must be recorded in CAB-TR:
   a. Name and staff/student ID number of the trainee
   b. Date(s) of training
   c. Title of the training module(s) completed, including the version number of the training material used
   d. Name and signature of the trainer
   e. Date of the most recent competency assessment and the outcome (Pass / Fail / Conditional Pass)
   f. Date of expiry of the authorisation, if applicable
4. Authorisation to enter the BSL-3 laboratory is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of the last competency assessment. After this period, the person must undergo a refresher training and a new competency assessment before being allowed to enter again.
5. If a person's authorisation has lapsed, the Laboratory Manager will mark the record as "Expired" in the status column. The person must not enter the laboratory until the record is updated to "Active" following successful completion of the refresher training.
6. Training records are considered confidential personnel information. Access to the records is restricted to the Laboratory Manager, the Principal Investigator, and the individual to whom the record pertains. Third parties may view the records only with the written consent of the individual or as required by the Institutional Biosafety Committee or other regulatory authority.
7. The Laboratory Manager will review all CAB-TR records at the start of each calendar month and notify any person whose authorisation will expire within the next 60 days. It is the responsibility of the individual to arrange for refresher training before the expiry date.

documents.content:
1.1 This policy establishes the framework for the safe handling, storage, transfer, and disposal of biological agents and toxins within all facilities under the purview of the Centre for Advanced Biosciences (CAB).

1.2 The policy is intended to protect personnel, the public, and the environment from biological hazards while supporting the legitimate research and teaching activities of the Centre.

1.3 All activities involving biological materials shall be conducted in accordance with the Singapore Biosafety Guidelines and the Biological Agents and Toxins Act (BATA) and its subsidiary legislation.

**2. Scope**

2.1 This policy applies to all CAB staff, students, visiting researchers, contractors, and any other persons engaged in work within CAB laboratories or using CAB-controlled biological materials.

2.2 The policy covers all work involving:
   (a) Human, animal, and plant pathogens;
   (b) Genetically modified organisms (GMOs) and genetically modified micro-organisms (GMMOs);
   (c) Biological toxins;
   (d) Human and primate cell lines, tissues, and blood products;
   (e) Any other biological material determined by the Biosafety Committee to present a biosafety risk.

2.3 This policy does not apply to:
   (a) Chemical safety matters, which are governed by the Chemical Safety Policy (CAB-POL-2023-07);
   (b) Radiation safety matters, which are governed by the Radiation Safety Policy (CAB-POL-2023-09);
   (c) Clinical activities conducted by the associated teaching hospital, which fall under hospital policy.

**3. Definitions**

3.1 **Biological Agent**: Any micro-organism, cell culture, or human endoparasite, including any that have been genetically modified, which may cause infection, allergy, toxicity, or otherwise pose a risk to human health.

CAB Policy Document 2024-01 effective_date 2024-03-15 date. Record status: historical.

3.2 **Biosafety Level (BSL)**: The containment level required for work with biological agents, as defined in the WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual, ranging from BSL-1 (lowest risk) to BSL-4 (highest risk).

3.3 **Biosafety Committee (BSC)**: The committee established by CAB to oversee biosafety matters, approve work with biological agents, and ensure compliance with this policy.

3.4 **Centre for Advanced Biosciences (CAB)**: The administrative unit to which the laboratories and facilities covered by this policy belong.

3.5 **Office of Safety, Health and Environment (OSHE)**: The office responsible for the day-to-day implementation of safety policies, including biosafety, across CAB.

3.6 **Principal Investigator (PI)**: The individual responsible for the scientific direction and operational conduct of a research group or laboratory within CAB.

3.7 **Biological Materials**: Any biological agent, toxin, GMO, or material containing or derived from the above, including clinical samples, environmental isolates, and research stocks.

3.8 **Containment**: The combination of physical, operational, and procedural measures used to prevent the release of biological agents from a laboratory or facility.

**4. General Biosafety Principles**

4.1 **Risk Assessment**: No work with biological materials shall commence until a documented risk assessment has been completed and approved. The risk assessment shall consider the hazard group of the agent, the proposed manipulations, the volume and concentration of material, the potential for aerosol generation, and the competence of personnel.

Compliance with this policy is a condition of access to CAB facilities. The Institutional Biosafety Committee (IBC) is responsible for approving amendments to this policy and for ensuring that it remains aligned with national and international biosafety standards.

---

### 2. Definitions

For the purposes of this policy:

- **Biorisk**: The combination of the probability of occurrence of harm and the severity of that harm, where the source of harm is a biological agent or toxin.
- **Biorisk Management**: A systematic approach to controlling biorisks, including risk assessment, risk mitigation, and performance monitoring.
- **Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC)**: A primary containment device that provides personnel, product, and environmental protection through HEPA filtration and directional airflow.
- **Competency Assessment**: A documented evaluation of an individual's ability to perform specific tasks safely and correctly.
- **Laboratory Safety Officer (LSO)**: The individual designated by the IBC to oversee day-to-day biosafety compliance, training coordination, and biorisk assessment activities.
- **PPE**: Personal Protective Equipment.

---

### 3. Biorisk Management

#### 3.1 General Principles

CAB adopts a biorisk management approach that considers the full range of risks associated with biological materials, including risks to personnel, the community, and the environment. This approach is based on the following principles:

a) Risk assessment shall be conducted before any new activity involving biological agents is initiated, and shall be reviewed whenever there is a significant change in the activity, the agents used, or the facility.

b) Risk mitigation measures shall be proportionate to the level of risk identified and shall follow the hierarchy of controls: elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, and PPE.

c) Biorisk assessments shall be documented and retained for at least five years. The LSO shall maintain a register of all completed assessments.

#### 3.2 Risk Assessment Process

The risk assessment process shall include:

CAB Policy Document 2025-01 effective_date 2025-01-15 date. Record status: current.

a) Identification of all biological agents and toxins present or potentially present in the sample or material;

b) Consideration of the agent's pathogenicity, virulence, route of transmission, and infectious dose;

c) Evaluation of the experimental procedures, including potential for aerosol generation, sharps use, and volume of material handled;

d) Assessment of personnel competency and training status;

e) Review of facility design and engineering controls, including BSC certification status and laboratory ventilation;

f) Identification of any additional risks, such as the presence of allergens, adventitious agents, or antibiotic resistance markers.

#### 3.3 Risk Mitigation

Following risk assessment, the following measures shall be applied as appropriate:

a) Use of the lowest possible biosafety level that is consistent with safe work;

b) Implementation of standard microbiological practices and, where required, additional special practices;

c) Use of appropriate containment equipment, including BSCs and centrifuge safety cups;

d) Restriction of access to the laboratory to authorised personnel only;

e) Posting of biohazard warning signs at laboratory entrances;

f) Development of activity-specific standard operating procedures (SOPs) when the risk assessment indicates a need.

###### 5.6 Follow-Up and Closure

Corrective actions identified in an audit report shall be tracked in the Biosafety Management System action log. The Principal Investigator or other responsible person named in the report shall submit a written response within 10 working days of receiving the report, stating the corrective actions taken or planned, and the target date for completion.

The audit team, or a nominee of the CAB Director, shall verify the implementation of corrective actions within 30 working days of the stated completion date. Where verification confirms that the corrective actions have been effectively implemented, the non-conformity shall be closed and recorded as such in the action log. Where implementation is found to be incomplete or ineffective, the matter shall be escalated to the Biosafety Committee for further direction.

The CAB Director shall review the audit findings and the status of corrective actions at least once per quarter, and shall report significant trends or recurring non-conformities to the Biosafety Committee.

#### 6. TRANSPORT OF BIOLOGICAL MATERIALS

###### 6.1 Scope

This Section applies to the transport of biological materials, including infectious substances, diagnostic specimens, genetically modified organisms, and other materials that may present a risk to human health, animal health, or the environment, within the University campus, between University premises, and to or from external parties.

Transport includes movement by road, rail, air, or sea, and includes the transfer of materials between laboratories, to or from storage facilities, and to or from collaborating institutions, couriers, or waste disposal contractors.

###### 6.2 General Requirements

All transport of biological materials shall be conducted in accordance with the applicable national and international regulations, including the Singapore Infectious Diseases Act, the UN Model Regulations, the International Air Transport Association (IATA) Dangerous Goods Regulations, and the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Technical Instructions.

The shipper of any biological material is responsible for:

a) Determining the correct classification of the material, including the UN number, proper shipping name, and packing group, where applicable;

b) Confirming that the material is correctly packaged and labelled;

c) Preparing the required documentation, including the shipper's declaration and any permits or licences; and

d) Ensuring that the transport is undertaken by an approved carrier and that the recipient is authorised to receive the material.

The Principal Investigator or Laboratory Manager shall ensure that all staff involved in the preparation, packaging, or dispatch of biological materials are trained in the relevant requirements before carrying out any transport-related duties. Training shall be recorded in accordance with the training record CAB-TR.

###### 6.3 Classification of Biological Materials

For the purposes of this Policy, biological materials transported off campus shall be classified as follows:

| Category | Description | Examples |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Category A | Infectious substances transported in a form that, when exposure to it occurs, is capable of causing permanent disability, life-threatening or fatal disease in otherwise healthy humans or animals | Cultures of pathogens assigned to Risk Group 3 or 4 |
| Category B | Infectious substances that do not meet the criteria for inclusion in Category A | Clinical specimens and cultures of Risk Group 2 agents |
| Exempt | Materials that are unlikely to cause disease in humans or animals, or that have been treated to eliminate pathogens | Fixed tissues, nucleic acid extracts, non-infectious cell lines |

**7.1 Purpose of This Section**

This section establishes the procedures for reviewing, amending, and versioning this Policy. The intent is to ensure that the Policy remains current, accurate, and aligned with national legislation, international standards, and the operational needs of the University. All amendments, whether substantive or editorial, shall be processed and recorded in accordance with this section.

**7.2 Scheduled Review Cycle**

The Policy shall be subject to a formal review at least once every three years from the date of the last comprehensive review. The next scheduled review shall be completed no later than 15 January 2028.

The Biosafety Committee (BSC) shall initiate the review. The BSC may, at its discretion, bring forward the review date if any of the following circumstances arise:

a) A significant incident involving biological materials occurs within the University or at another institution that reveals a gap or deficiency in this Policy;

b) A relevant national law, regulation, or code of practice is amended or introduced;

c) A relevant international guideline, such as those issued by the World Health Organization (WHO) Laboratory Biosafety Manual, is updated; or

d) The BSC otherwise determines that a review is necessary to address an emerging risk or operational issue.

**7.3 Initiation of Amendments**

Any member of the University community, including staff, students, and researchers, may propose an amendment to this Policy. Proposals shall be submitted in writing to the CAB Office using the Amendment Request Form (CAB-FM-07). The form shall include:

a) The name and contact details of the proposer;

b) The section(s) of the Policy to which the proposed amendment relates;

c) A clear statement of the proposed change, including the current text and the proposed revised text where practicable;

d) The rationale for the change, including any supporting evidence, references, or incident reports; and

e) The signature of the proposer and, where the proposer is a student, the endorsement of their Principal Investigator or Supervisor.

The CAB Office shall acknowledge receipt of the Amendment Request Form within five (5) working days. The CAB Office shall maintain a register of all amendment requests, which shall be reviewed by the BSC at its next scheduled meeting.

**7.4 Review by the Biosafety Committee**

The BSC shall consider all amendment requests received. In reviewing a proposed amendment, the BSC shall have regard to:

a) The safety implications of the proposed change;

b) Consistency with national legislation and international standards;

c) The operational practicality of the proposed change for the University's research and teaching activities;

d) The resource implications, including any training, equipment, or facility modifications that may be required; and

e) Any comments or advice received from the CAB Office, the Office of Safety, Health and Environment (OSHE), or other relevant parties.

The BSC may approve an amendment, approve it with modifications, defer it for further information or consultation, or reject it. The decision of the BSC shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting and communicated to the proposer in writing by the CAB Office within ten (10) working days of the decision.

**7.5 Approval of Amendments**

documents.title: CAB Standard Operating Procedure 2024-01: BSL-3 Laboratory Entry and Exit
documents.content:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the mandatory sequence for personnel entering and exiting the BSL-3 laboratory located at Level 3, Wing B, CAB. It ensures that all personnel maintain the containment barrier, follow the airlock protocol, and properly use personal protective equipment (PPE) to prevent accidental exposure to biological agents.

2. SCOPE

This SOP applies to all CAB staff, students, and approved external collaborators who require access to the BSL-3 laboratory. It does not apply to maintenance personnel performing work inside the containment suite unless they have completed the required BSL-3 training and have been granted access by the Laboratory Manager.

3. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| BSL-3 | Biosafety Level 3 |
| CAB | Centre for Advanced Biosafety |
| PPE | Personal Protective Equipment |
| Airlock | A chamber with interlocked doors providing a controlled transition between the corridor and the containment area |
| Dirty Side | The corridor side of the airlock, considered non-contained |
| Clean Side | The laboratory interior side of the airlock, considered contained |
| Buddy System | A practice where two persons are present in the laboratory during high-risk operations |

4. RESPONSIBILITIES

4.1 Laboratory Manager (T. Rajah) – Ensures that this SOP is current, that all personnel are trained, and that PPE supplies are always available.

4.2 Biosafety Officer (B. Tan) – Reviews this SOP annually, conducts audits, and investigates any breach of containment.

4.3 All Personnel – Must follow this SOP without deviation. Any deviation must be reported immediately to the Laboratory Manager and the Biosafety Officer.

CAB Standard Operating Procedure 2024-01 effective_date 2024-06-20 date. Record status: historical.

5. PPE REQUIREMENTS

The following PPE is mandatory for all personnel inside the BSL-3 laboratory:

- Disposable surgical scrubs (provided by CAB)
- Dedicated laboratory shoes (closed-toe, non-slip)
- Disposable boot covers
- Full-length, disposable gown (back-closing)
- Double gloves (inner nitrile, outer nitrile)
- N95 respirator (fit-tested) or powered air-purifying respirator (PAPR) if approved by the Biosafety Officer
- Full-face shield over the respirator

PPE must be donned in the order listed above and doffed in the reverse order, except that the outer gloves and gown are removed together in the airlock as described in Section 7.

6. ENTRY PROCEDURE

Entry into the BSL-3 laboratory is a two-stage process: preparation in the change room, followed by passage through the airlock.

6.1 Stage 1 – Preparation in the Change Room

1. Confirm that you have signed the entry logbook at the reception desk and that your name is listed on the daily access roster.
2. Remove all personal clothing and jewellery. Store them in your assigned locker.
3. Put on the disposable surgical scrubs. Ensure the scrubs are clean and free of any visible tears.
4. Put on the dedicated laboratory shoes.
5. Put on the N95 respirator. Perform a user seal check:
   - Cover the respirator with both hands and exhale sharply. If air leaks around the nose, adjust the nosepiece.
   - Cover the respirator with both hands and inhale. If the respirator collapses slightly, the seal is acceptable.
6. Put on the inner nitrile gloves.
7. Inspect the outer gloves, gown, boot covers, and face shield for any defects before proceeding to the airlock.

documents.title: CAB Standard Operating Procedure 2024-01: BSL-3 Laboratory Entry and Exit
documents.content:
1. Complete your work and decontaminate all materials that will leave the laboratory (see Section 9, Waste Handling).
2. Approach the airlock from the laboratory side. Verify that the indicator light shows GREEN.
3. Open the inner door, step inside, and close the door fully behind you. Wait for the light to turn GREEN again.
4. Remove the outer gloves and the gown together. Peel the gown off from the shoulders, turning it inside out as you go, and place both items into the biohazard waste bin inside the airlock.
5. Remove the boot covers and place them into the same bin.
6. Remove the full-face shield and place it on the clean shelf for disinfection after exiting.
7. Open the outer door and step into the change room. Close the door behind you.
8. Proceed to Section 8, Doffing and Exit, for the remaining steps.

Note: If the alarm sounds while you are inside the airlock, remain still. Do not open either door. Wait for instructions from the Laboratory Manager or Biosafety Officer over the intercom.

8. DOFFING AND EXIT

1. In the change room, remove the inner nitrile gloves first. Dispose of them in the yellow biohazard bin.
2. Perform hand hygiene using the alcohol-based hand rub dispenser on the wall.
3. Remove the N95 respirator. Grasp the bottom strap, then the top strap, and lift the respirator away from your face without touching the front. Dispose of it in the yellow bin.
4. Remove the surgical scrubs and place them in the linen collection hamper labelled "CAB – LAUNDRY".
5. Remove the dedicated laboratory shoes and place them on the shoe rack. These shoes must not be worn outside the laboratory area.
6. Perform hand hygiene again.
7. Sign out in the exit logbook at the reception desk. Record the time of exit and confirm that you have not removed any items from the laboratory without prior authorisation.

9. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES

Emergency procedures apply to all personnel inside the BSL-3 laboratory. In the event of any emergency, the primary priority is the safety of personnel. Containment of the agent is secondary but must be addressed as soon as it is safe to do so.

9.1 Spill Response

CAB Standard Operating Procedure 2024-01 version_number 1.0 version. Record status: historical.

Spills are categorised according to the volume of the spill and the risk of aerosol generation.

1. Alert others in the laboratory by calling out "Spill on the bench" clearly.
2. Cover the spill with absorbent paper towels.
3. Carefully pour freshly prepared 1% sodium hypochlorite solution over the towels, working from the outside of the spill towards the centre.
4. Allow the disinfectant to remain in contact for at least 20 minutes.
5. Wipe up the spill with the towels and place them in the biohazard waste bin.
6. Wipe the area again with 70% ethanol.
7. Complete an entry in the incident report log CAB-IRL within 24 hours.

9.1.2 Large Spills (10 mL or More, or Any Aerosol)

1. Immediately leave the laboratory, following the exit procedure in Section 7.2. Do not attempt to clean the spill yourself.
2. Alert the Laboratory Manager and the Biosafety Officer by calling the emergency number 6772-8890 from a safe location.
3. Do not re-enter the laboratory until the Biosafety Officer has assessed the situation and given clearance.
4. The Biosafety Officer will coordinate the cleanup, which will be performed by trained personnel wearing full PPE and using a respirator.
5. Complete an entry in the incident report log CAB-IRL as soon as possible, but no later than 4 hours after the incident.

1. PURPOSE

This SOP describes the procedures for entry into and exit from the BSL-3 laboratory located on
Level 2 of the CAB Annex. The procedures are designed to prevent the release of biological agents
and to protect personnel from exposure.

2. SCOPE

This SOP applies to all personnel, including researchers, technicians, students, and visitors,
who require access to the BSL-3 laboratory. Access is granted only to personnel who have
completed the required biosafety training and have been approved by the Biosafety Officer.

3. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS

|---|---|
| BSL-3 | Biosafety Level 3 |
| CAB | Containment and Biosafety |

5. PPE REQUIREMENTS

The following PPE must be worn by all personnel inside the BSL-3 laboratory. PPE is stored on
shelves outside the laboratory, on the left of the airlock entrance.

| Item | Quantity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Disposable gown (fluid-resistant) | 1 | Must be worn over laboratory clothing. |
| Inner gloves (nitrile) | 1 pair | Must be worn under the outer gloves. |
| Outer gloves (nitrile) | 1 pair | Must be worn over the cuffs of the gown. |
| Surgical mask | 1 | Must be worn at all times. |
| Shoe covers | 1 pair | Must be worn over closed-toe shoes. |

Double gloving is mandatory for all work involving open manipulation of infectious material.
This includes, but is not limited to, pipetting, vortexing, and opening tubes containing
concentrated cultures. For work that does not involve open manipulation, such as operating
equipment behind a closed front, single gloving is permitted.

The entry procedure is a sequence of steps that must be followed in order. Do not skip steps.
If you are unsure about any step, stop and ask the Laboratory Manager or Biosafety Officer.

6.1 Before Entering the Laboratory Area

documents.title: CAB Standard Operating Procedure 2024-01: BSL-3 Laboratory Entry and Exit
documents.content:
6.1 Before Entering the Laboratory Area

1. Remove all personal items (watches, jewellery, mobile phones, wallets) and place them in the
   personal lockers provided outside the laboratory. Lockers are located along the corridor
   opposite the main door, labelled A1 to A24.
2. Change out of outdoor footwear into the laboratory-issued closed-toe shoes kept on the shoe
   rack. Outdoor footwear must be placed in the shoe cubbies provided. Do not walk in socks or
   barefoot in this area.
3. Check the daily entry roster posted on the notice board to confirm that your name has been
   cleared for the day's work. If your name is not on the roster, do not proceed. Contact the
   Laboratory Manager for verification.
4. Review the risk assessment form CAB-RAF for the specific activity you will be performing. A
   copy of the current CAB-RAF is kept in the clear file holder next to the roster. If the
   activity you are about to perform is not covered by a current CAB-RAF, stop and inform the
   Biosafety Officer before proceeding.
5. Sign the entry logbook. Record the date, time of entry, your name (in block letters), and the
   purpose of entry. The logbook is located on the small table to the right of the airlock door.
   Use the pen attached to the table; do not bring pens into the laboratory.
6. Perform a visual inspection of the airlock anteroom. Check that the inner door is closed and
   the pressure differential gauge reads between -30 Pa and -50 Pa relative to the corridor.
   If the gauge reads outside this range, do not enter. Notify the Laboratory Manager
   immediately.
7. If you are entering to perform work involving open manipulation of infectious material,
   ensure that you have sufficient supplies for the entire session before entering. Once inside,
   do not exit and re-enter for supplies unless absolutely necessary.

6.2 Donning PPE

1. Collect the required PPE from the shelves outside the laboratory, on the left of the airlock
   entrance. Check the size and condition of each item. Discard any item that appears torn,
   perforated, or expired in the designated waste bin labelled "PPE waste".
2. Put on the disposable gown first. Ensure the gown covers the back and front of your body and
   that the ties are secured at the back. The gown must be long enough to cover your laboratory
   clothing completely.
3. Put on the shoe covers over your closed-toe shoes. Pull them up over the ankles. If you feel
   any tear, replace them before proceeding.
4. Put on the inner gloves (nitrile). Ensure they fit snugly. Do not wear rings or other
   jewellery under the gloves.
5. Put on the surgical mask. The mask must cover both your nose and mouth. Press the nose wire
   to fit the contour of your nose. Do not remove the mask while inside the laboratory.
6. Put on the safety goggles or face shield. Adjust the strap so that the goggles sit firmly but
   comfortably. If you wear prescription glasses, the goggles must fit over them without
   causing gaps.
7. Put on the outer gloves (nitrile). Tuck the cuffs of the gown into the outer gloves so that
   no skin is exposed at the wrists.
8. Perform a buddy check. Ask another person who is entering or a person already inside the
   laboratory to verify that your PPE is complete and that there are no gaps or exposed skin.
   If you are entering alone, use the full-length mirror mounted on the inside of the airlock
   door to perform the check yourself.

CAB Standard Operating Procedure 2024-01: BSL-3 Laboratory Entry and Exit

7. Documentation and Record-Keeping

7.1 Entry Log

1. Every person entering the BSL-3 laboratory must sign the entry log before donning PPE. The log is located on the clipboard holder immediately to the left of the airlock door, outside the laboratory.
2. Record the following information legibly in the designated columns:
   a. Date and time of entry (use the 24-hour clock, e.g. 09:15, 14:40)
   b. Full name and staff/student ID number
   c. Purpose of entry (e.g. routine culture work, equipment maintenance, cleaning)
   d. Time of exit
   e. Initials of the person performing the buddy check, if applicable
3. If you forget to sign in before entering, do not attempt to enter again solely to sign the log. Upon exiting, sign the log and clearly state the actual time of entry in the remarks column, and inform the Laboratory Manager within the same working day.
4. Do not leave blank columns. If a column is not applicable, write "N/A" in that column.
5. The entry log is a controlled document. Do not remove pages from the logbook. When a logbook is full, return it to the Laboratory Manager, who will archive it in the records room (Cabinet B, shelf 3).
6. Electronic entry logs may be maintained in place of the paper log, subject to prior approval by the Laboratory Manager. The electronic system must capture the same fields listed in clause 7.1.2 and must not allow retrospective edits without an audit trail.

7.2 Training Records

1. No person may enter the BSL-3 laboratory unless their training record, CAB-TR, shows a current and valid authorisation for entry.
2. Training records are maintained by the Laboratory Manager and are updated within five working days of the completion of any training session or refresher course.
3. The following entries must be recorded in CAB-TR:
   a. Name and staff/student ID number of the trainee
   b. Date(s) of training
   c. Title of the training module(s) completed, including the version number of the training material used
   d. Name and signature of the trainer
   e. Date of the most recent competency assessment and the outcome (Pass / Fail / Conditional Pass)
   f. Date of expiry of the authorisation, if applicable
4. Authorisation to enter the BSL-3 laboratory is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of the last competency assessment. After this period, the person must undergo a refresher training and a new competency assessment before being allowed to enter again.
5. If a person's authorisation has lapsed, the Laboratory Manager will mark the record as "Expired" in the status column. The person must not enter the laboratory until the record is updated to "Active" following successful completion of the refresher training.
6. Training records are considered confidential personnel information. Access to the records is restricted to the Laboratory Manager, the Principal Investigator, and the individual to whom the record pertains. Third parties may view the records only with the written consent of the individual or as required by the Institutional Biosafety Committee or other regulatory authority.
7. The Laboratory Manager will review all CAB-TR records at the start of each calendar month and notify any person whose authorisation will expire within the next 60 days. It is the responsibility of the individual to arrange for refresher training before the expiry date.
